You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testExtremeValues` is designed to verify the cumulative probabilities of a Normal distribution for extreme values both very negative and very positive, ensuring that there should be no convergence exceptions thrown and probabilities are within expected ranges.

The failure is caused by a `ConvergenceException` (specifically a `MaxIterationsExceededException`) thrown from the `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double)` method. This method tries to calculate the cumulative probability using the error function `Erf.erf()` inside a try block.

If `Erf.erf()` fails by throwing `MaxIterationsExceededException`, the code in the catch block runs. The catch block has special handling for very large or small input x values, returning 0 when `x` is sufficiently smaller than the mean (by 20 standard deviations), and returns 1 when `x` is sufficiently greater than mean (by 20 standard deviations). For values within this range, it rethrows the exception.

The failure in the test indicates that for some extreme values (likely beyond the -9 to 9 range tested or potentially near Double.MAX_VALUE in the last assert), the erf function does not converge causing the exception to be thrown. Since the test expects no exceptions, this leads to test failure.

Therefore, the underlying cause is that very extreme input values to `cumulativeProbability()` cause the nested `Erf.erf()` calculation to fail convergence and throw `MaxIterationsExceededException`. The current catch only handles values beyond ±20 standard deviations gracefully by returning 0 or 1. Values inside that range, even if numerically challenging, cause exceptions.

The test code loop is going to i=100 and tests cumulativeProbability at ±i, so for i > 20, the catch block should handle by returning 0 or 1 and prevent exceptions. However, since the test fails, it means either some values inside ±20 standard deviations range cause the iteration failure or the method is not properly guarding against extreme values or non-finite inputs like ±Infinity which may occur in other reported test cases (mentioned in bug report).

In summary, the bug occurs because the error function erf in the cumulativeProbability calculation can fail on convergence for extreme input values. The defensive catch fallback only returns 0 or 1 for x beyond ±20 standard deviations; otherwise, it propagates the exception leading to the observed failure.

Recent bug reports about decimal precision or regression are not relevant here since this is about convergence exceptions during cumulative probability calculation.

The likely fix should involve improving handling of extreme inputs in `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability()` and/or making `Erf.erf()` more robust or replaced with higher precision approximation for extreme values to avoid `MaxIterationsExceededException`. The main method needing fix is `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double)`.

Hence, the root cause is the propagation of `MaxIterationsExceededException` from the `Erf.erf` call for difficult extreme arguments inside the ±20 standard deviations boundary, leading to unhandled exceptions in normal cumulative probability calculations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
